newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Handelsblatt EMU poll sees rising certainty.
newsitem.headline: German Handelsblatt EMU poll sees rising certainty.

text.p: The latest monthly survey of financial experts by the German business daily Handelsblatt points to increasing confidence that European economic and monetary union (EMU) will begin punctually in 1999.
In an advance report ahead of publication on Friday, Handelsblatt said its "EMU barometer" measuring optimism in a timely start of EMU rose to 79 percent in January from 76 percent in December.
The paper gave no details about the basis for the poll.
Most of those polled by the paper said they were encouraged by the increasing political will in Europe to qualify for EMU and to introduce the single currency in 1999.

Concerns that many European Union members might not meet the tough fiscal criteria and qualify for EMU in the first round were becoming less important in light of the demonstrated political commitment to the euro.

The current dispute between Germany and France over the independance of the future European Central Bank was seen by many of those polled as disruptive in the run up to EMU, but they added that the discussion should not be overrated. REUTER
